content: A plane joint, also known as a gliding joint, arthrodial joint, or plane articulation, is a type of synovial joint that permits only gliding movements. This joint allows one bone to slide over the surface of another bone. For example, the gliding joint in the wrist enables flexion of the wrist and facilitates very small lateral (side-to-side) movements. Similarly, gliding joints are also present in the ankles, contributing to their mobility. As a synovial joint, the gliding joint is characterized by its ability to allow a significant range of motion compared to other joint types.
